quiz.q: Ailerons control…
quiz.why: They deflect in opposite directions on each wing.

quiz.q: For pitch stability the CG must be…
quiz.why: Positive static margin.

quiz.q: A static margin of 0.15 means…
quiz.why: Positive margin.

quiz.q: Dynamic stability concerns…
quiz.why: Whether oscillations die out.

quiz.q: Statically stable means the oscillation dies out.
quiz.why: That is dynamic stability; static stability is the initial tendency.

quiz.q: More stability is always better.
quiz.why: Too much makes control heavy and wastes trim drag.

quiz.q: The CG can be anywhere as long as the wing lifts.
quiz.why: An aft CG makes the aircraft unstable.

quiz.q: The neutral point is at 40% of the mean chord and the CG at 25%. Find the static margin.
quiz.why: 0.15, or 15%: stable.

quiz.q: A glider has a 50 g wing at x = 10 cm, a 10 g tail at x = 40 cm and 20 g of nose weight at x = 0. Find the CG.
quiz.why: x_cg = 11.25 cm from the nose.

quiz.q: For the Example 6.2 glider (mean chord 8 cm), the neutral point is at 13 cm. Is it stable?
quiz.why: SM ≈ 0.22: stable. Remove nose weight and the CG moves aft toward instability.

quiz.q: In Example 6.2, how much nose weight m puts the CG at 12 cm?
The elevator, on the horizontal tail.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit. Which surface controls pitch?

quiz.q: SM = −0.02 < 0: statically unstable.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit. CG at 30% chord, neutral point at 28%. Stable?

quiz.q: Its CG is too far aft, near or behind the neutral point.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit. Why does a paper airplane with no nose weight pitch up and stall?

quiz.q: Stability margins cost fuel: a conventional tail usually pushes down to balance the aircraft, and the wing must make extra lift, with extra drag, to carry it. Trimming that penalty is part of the efficient-aircraft path NASA describes.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit.

quiz.q: The same balance and control ideas keep Earth-observing satellites pointed steadily so their instruments can map the planet.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit.

quiz.q: An aircraft rotates about its center of gravity: pitch (elevator), roll (ailerons), yaw (rudder).
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit.

quiz.q: Static stability: after a disturbance, the aircraft initially tends to return. Dynamic stability: the motion actually dies out over time.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit.

quiz.q: Pitch stability needs the center of gravity ahead of the neutral point. Static margin = (x_np − x_cg)/c̄ must be positive.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit.

quiz.q: A tail far behind the CG works like the feathers on an arrow: a nose-up disturbance raises the tail’s lift and pushes the nose back down.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit.
